paper_title: Acyclic, Star and Injective Colouring: A Complexity Picture for H-Free Graphs

statement: The basic idea (Case 1) is as follows. Let G be an instance of Acyclic 3-Colouring. We pick an edge uv ∈ E(G). In G − uv we “glue” F 0 by identifying u with x and y with v; see also Figure 1. We then prove that G has an acyclic 3-colouring if and only if G0 has an acyclic 3-colouring. Then, by performing the same operation for each other edge of G as well, we obtain a graph G00 , such that G has an acyclic 3-colouring if and only if G00 has so. As the size of G00 is polynomial in the size of G and the girth of G00 is at least g, we have proven the theorem. The challenge in this technique is that we do not know how the graph F 0 looks. We can only prove its existence and therefore have to consider several possibilities for the properties of the acyclic 3-colourings of F 0 . Hence, we distinguish between Cases 1–3, 4a, and 4b. u=x
context: Proof. We reduce from Acyclic 3-Colouring, which is known to be NP-complete [14]. We start by taking a graph F that has a 4-colouring but no 3-colouring and that is of girth at least g. By a seminal result of Erdős [18], such a graph F exists (and its size is constant, as it only depends on g which is a fixed integer). We now repeatedly remove edges from F until we obtain a graph F 0 that is acyclically 3-colourable. Let xy be the last edge that we removed. As F has no 3-colouring, the edge xy exists. Moreover, by our construction, the graph F 0 + xy is not acyclically 3-colourable. As edge deletions do not decrease the girth, F 0 + xy and F 0 have girth at least g.
